English Literature.question: ১) “There is nothing either good or bad, but thinking makes it so.” is a quotation of -
English Literature.exp: This quote is taken from the “Act 2: Scene 2” of Hamlet written by William Shakespeare. The dialogue is uttered by Hamlet.

English Literature.question: ২) “Cavalier poets” was seen in which English Literary period?
English Literature.exp:
Cavalier poet, any of a group of English gentlemen poets, called Cavaliers because of their loyalty to Charles I (1625–49) during the English Civil Wars, as opposed to Roundheads, who supported Parliament.
As we know that the 'Caroline Period' is named after the name of King Charles -1.
This group included -
- Richard Lovelace
- Sir John Suckling
- Robert Herrick
- Thomas Carew.

These poets are also called the son of Ben as they were the admirers and followers of Ben Jonson.

Source: Britannica.com

English Literature.question: ৩) A narrative poem that tells a story through dialogue and action -
English Literature.exp:
Ballad:
A narrative poem that tells a story through dialogue and action. Its general features are:
- It is narrative in form, and so, it tells a story.
- Its narrator is generally impersonal third person.
- It opens dramatically at the middle of the story.
- Its story is told in dialogue and action.

Elegy:
A lyric poem mourning for the death of an individual or lamenting over a tragic event.
Ode:
An exalted lyric poem that begins with an address to someone, instil anguish in the middle part and ends with consolation.
Lyric:
A short poem expressing personal or subjective thoughts and intense feelings of a single speaker. It is identical to a song sung with a lyre.

Source: An ABC of English Literature - Dr M Mofizar Rahman

English Literature.question:
৪) ''My heart aches, and a drowsy numbness pains
My sense, as though of hemlock I had drunk'.'
- Who wrote these lines?
English Literature.exp:
My heart aches, and a drowsy numbness pains
My sense, as though of hemlock I had drunk,

Or emptied some dull opiate to the drains
One minute past, and Lethe-wards had sunk:

’Tis not through envy of thy happy lot,
But being too happy in thine happiness,

That thou, light-wingèd Dryad of the trees,
In some melodious plot
Of beechen green, and shadows numberless,
Singest of summer in full-throated ease.

- Ode to a Nightingale
By John Keats.

English Literature.question: ৫) A story about a semi-god human figure -
English Literature.exp:
Legend:
A story about a semi-god human figure. In it writer focuses on the greatness of a human being though some supernatural beings may be involved in it.
Beowulf, King Arther, Faust and Rabin Hood are the great legendary figures.

Myth:
An Ancient story about God and Goddesses and their mysterious activities.
Mythology:
Myths are collectively called mythology. Greek, Roman, Egyptian, Indian mythology are well known.

Source: An ABC of English Literature by Dr. M Mofizar Rahman.

English Literature.question: ৬) A literary form in which one story is told in the guise of another story is called -
English Literature.exp:
Allegory: (রূপক বর্ণনা; প্রতীকাশ্রয়ী কাহিনী)
A literary form in which one story is told in the guise of another story.
Ex: Bunyan's Pilgrim's Progress 

Novelette:
A short novel usually of thirty to forty thousand words. It is shorter than a novel but longer than a short story.
Non-fiction:
Fictitious narratives in prose.
Satire:
A literary attack on the follies and vices of an individual or a society with a view to correcting them through laughter and ridicule is known as satire. It may be in prose or in verse.

Source: An ABC of English Literature by Dr. M Mofizar Rahman.

English Literature.question: ৭) 'Albatross' is a character created by -
English Literature.exp:
The Rime of the Ancient Mariner, a poem in seven parts by Samuel Taylor Coleridge that first appeared in Lyrical Ballads, published collaboratively by Coleridge and William Wordsworth in 1798.
The title character detains one of three young men on their way to a wedding feast and mesmerizes him with the story of his youthful experience at sea—his slaughter of an albatross, the deaths of his fellow sailors, his suffering, and his eventual redemption.

The important characters of this work are - The Mariner, Wedding Guest, Albatross, The Nightmare, Life in Death.

Source: Britannica.com

English Literature.question: ৮) In which English literary period, the ‘prose’ was introduced?
English Literature.exp:
The 'Prose' was introduced in The Anglo-Saxon/Old English Period.

- Alfred the Great who reigned over England from 871 to 901 encouraged education and supervised the compilation of 'The Anglo Saxon Chronicle'.
- The Anglo Saxon Chronicle is the earliest prose of English Literature.

Source: An ABC of English Literature by Dr. M Mofizar Rahman.

English Literature.question: ৯) The term ‘Parable’ in literature teaches -
English Literature.exp:
Parable: (নীতিগর্ভ রূপককাহিনি; রূপক)
An allegorical story of human characters which teaches a religious moral. There are several famous parables in the Bible.
It teaches God's supremacy and His ways to man.
Source: An ABC of English Literature by Dr. M Mofizar Rahman.

English Literature.question: ১০) ‘The Augustan Age’ is also known as -
English Literature.exp:
The Neoclassical Period was the fourth English Literary Period.
The duration of the period was - 1660 to 1785.

This period was divided into 3 sub-period which are as follows:
1. The Restoration Period (1660 - 1700)
2. The Augustan Period or The Age of Pope (1700-1745)
3. The Age of Sensibility or The Age of Johnson (1745 - 1785)

Source: An ABC of English Literature by Dr. M Mofizar Rahman.

English Literature.question: ১১) Which Shakespeare’s tragedy is known as revenge tragedy?
English Literature.exp:
Revenge Tragedy:
Revenge tragedy is a kind of tragedy that presents a quest for vengeance and results in bloodshed and mutilation.
It is modelled on the Senecan tragedy. Thomas Kyd is considered to be the father of Revenge Tragedy.
It was popular in England during the late 16th century and 17th centuries with the Elizabethan and Jacobean.

Thomas Kyd's Spanish Tragedy; John Webster's Duchess of Malfi and Shakespeare's Hamlet are famous revenge tragedies.

Source: An ABC of English Literature by Dr. M Mofizar Rahman.

English Literature.question: ১২) “The Vision of Judgement” is a/an -
English Literature.exp:
The Vision of Judgment is a satirical poem in ottava rima by Lord Byron.
It contains a devastating parody of that poet laureate’s fulsome eulogy of King George III.

Lord Byron is considered to be the Rebel Poet and Byronic Hero in English Literature.
His other famous works are:
- Don Juan
- Childe Harold's Pilgrimage
- Hours of Idleness,
- Heaven and Earth etc.
Source: Britannica and An ABC of English Literature, Dr M Mofizar Rahman

English Literature.question: ১৩) Among the following periods, which one is contemporary?
English Literature.exp:
ইংরেজি সাহিত্যের যুগ বিভাগে সবচেয়ে সমসাময়িক যুগ হচ্ছে - The Post-Modern Period.
এটি ১৯৩৯ সালে শুরু হয়ে এখনো চলমান।

তার আগের যুগটি হচ্ছে - The Modern Period.
Modern Period এর আবার দুটি ভাগ রয়েছে। যথা -
1. The Edwardian Period (1901 - 1910)
2. The Georgian Period (1910 - 1936)
সুতরাং প্রশ্নে প্রদত্ত অপশনগুলোর মধ্যে The Georgian Period হচ্ছে সবচেয়ে সমসাময়িক।

Source: An ABC of English Literature by Dr. M Mofizar Rahman.

English Literature.question: ১৪) Charles Dickens was a writer of -
English Literature.exp:
Charles Dickens, in full Charles John Huffam Dickens, (born February 7, 1812, Portsmouth, Hampshire, England—died June 9, 1870.
He was one of the most famous novelists of the Victorian Period.

The duration of the Victorian Period was - 1832 - 1901.
Important writers of this period were -
- Alfred Tennyson
- Charles Darwin
- Edward Fitzgerald
- William Makepeace Thackeray
- Robert Browning
- Emily Bronte
- Karl Marx
- George Eliot
- Mathew Arnold
- Mark Twain
- Thomas Hardy

Source: An ABC of English Literature by Dr. M Mofizar Rahman.

English Literature.question: ১৫) Find the odd-one-out -
English Literature.exp:
Oscar Wilde was a Victorian Writer.
The rest are Modern Period's writer.

So, Oscar Wilde is the odd one here.

English Literature.question: ১৬) Who is known as a famous critic on Shakespeare?
English Literature.exp:
Andrew Cecil Bradley (1851-1935):
Andrew is a Modern writer in English Literature.

- He is better known as A. C Bradley, a famous critic on Shakespeare.
- His some literary works are:
1. Shakespearean Tragedy
2. Oxford Lectures on Poetry etc.

Source: An ABC of English Literature by Dr. M Mofizar Rahman.

English Literature.question: ১৭) ‘Lyric’ dominates the literary works of which period?
English Literature.exp:
The Romantic Period (1798 - 1832):
Some literary feature of this Age -
- Creative enthusiasm reached almost the level of the Elizabethan creative force.
- Subjective poetry replaces the objective poetry of the neoclassical period.
- It values common 'natural' man and rejects artificial urban life as the subject of poetry.
- Lyric poetry dominates.
- Myth reflects rebellious views against oppression, restraints, and controls.

Source: Britannica and An ABC of English Literature, Dr M Mofizar Rahman

English Literature.question:
১৮) “Some are born great, some achieve greatness, and some have greatness thrust upon them.”
Who said this?
English Literature.exp:
It is a famous quote from William Shakespeare.
The dialogue is taken from the act -2, scene - 5 of the play “Twelfth Night” and uttered by - Malvolio.

Source: Twelfth Night, William Shakespeare.

English Literature.question: ১৯) Which time frame known as “Shakespearean Age” -
English Literature.exp:
- Shakespeare had started writing in the Elizabethan Period wrote twelve serious plays in the Jacobean Period.
- Though Shakespeare wrote these serious plays in the Jacobean Age, he is called an Elizabethan dramatist and never the Jacobean.
- The period (1590 - 1616) in which he wrote his plays is called Shakespearean Age.
Source: An ABC of English Literature, Dr M Mofizar Rahman.

English Literature.question: ২০) “Hymn” is -
English Literature.option1: A lyric poem or song in praise of God or deity or a hero.
English Literature.option2: A lyric poem mourning for the death of an individual or lamenting over a tragic event.
English Literature.option3: A kind of lyric poem written to celebrate a wedding.
English Literature.option4: A literary motif in lyric poems.
English Literature.exp:
Hymn: (ঈশ্বরবন্দনা)
A lyric poem or song in praise of God or deity or a hero.
Elegy: (শোকগাথা)
A lyric poem mourning for the death of an individual or lamenting over a tragic event.
Epithalamion:
A kind of lyric poem written to celebrate a wedding.
Carpe Diem:
A literary motif in lyric poems.

Source: An ABC of English Literature by Dr. M Mofizar Rahman.

English Literature.question: ২১) In which English literary period, Prose in English gets a strong foundation?
English Literature.exp:
Main Literary Features of The Middle English Period:
- Poetry serves as the main genre.
- Prose in English gets a strong foundation.
- The English Language reaches a considerable standard though old spelling continues.
- Drama began in the form of 'Mystery Play', 'Morality Play' and 'Interlude'.
Source: An ABC of English Literature, Dr M Mofizar Rahman.

English Literature.question: ২২) Which one is the first romance in prose?
English Literature.exp:
Sir Thomas Malory is one of the major literary figure of the Middle English Period.
He wrote Morte d’Arthur (1485) which is the first romance in prose.

Source: An ABC of English Literature, Dr M Mofizar Rahman.

English Literature.question: ২৩) Which one is not a literary work of Geoffrey Chaucer?
English Literature.exp:
Geoffrey Chaucer (1340-1400):
The outstanding English poet before Shakespeare.
His 'The Canterbury Tales' ranks as one of the greatest poetic works in English.

His other notable works-
- 'Troilus and Criseyde',
- 'The Parlement of Foules',
- 'The Pardoner’s Tale',
- 'The Miller’s Tale',
- 'The Friar’s Tale',
- 'The Nun’s Priest’s Tale',
- 'The Clerk’s Tale',
- 'The Man of Law’s Tale',
- 'The Franklin’s Tale'.

N.B: Troilus and Cressida is a tragedy by William Shakespeare.

Source: Britannica.com

English Literature.question: ২৪) Which time frame is known as “Age of Sensibility”?
English Literature.exp:
The Neo-classical period (1660-1798) comprises three shorter ages:
1. The Restoration Period (1660-1700),
2. The Augustan Age or the Age of Pope (1700-1745) and
3. The Age of Sensibility or The Age of Johnson (1745-1798).

Source: An ABC of English Literature - Dr M Mofizar Rahman

English Literature.question: ২৫) Which one is not a literary work of “The Old English Period”?
English Literature.exp:
Literary works of the Old English Period:

'Beowulf' (the earliest epic in English),
'The Wanderer',
'The Seafarer',
'The Husband's Message',
'The Anglo-Saxon Chronicle' (the earliest prose of English literature)
are major literary works of the Old English period.

Confessio Amantis is a literary work of The Middle English Period which is written by John Grower.

Source: An ABC of English Literature - Dr M Mofizar Rahman

English Literature.question: ২৬) The Renaissance began at -
English Literature.exp:
Renaissance began in 1453. Though it's effect on English life and literature was left after 1500.
For this reason, it is generally accepted that the Renaissance Period began with the beginning of the 16th century and continued till the Restoration in 1660.
It means Renaissance English Literary Period began in 1500 and ended in 1660.

Source: An ABC of English Literature - Dr M Mofizar Rahman

English Literature.question:
২৭) 'The bride hath paced into the hall,
Red as a rose is she.'
It is an example of -
English Literature.exp:
Simile: (উপমা)
A simile is an explicit comparison between two different things.
Usually 'as' and 'like' are used in it.
The above example is Simile. It was taken from Coleridge's Ancient Mariner.

Soliloquy:
A dramatic technique of speaking alone on stage.
Stanza:
A division of a poem. It is a smaller unit of the structure of a poem.
Pyrrhic:
A foot of two unstressed syllables.

Source: An ABC of English Literature - Dr M Mofizar Rahman

English Literature.question: ২৮) ‘Kingdom of Nowhere’ is written by -
English Literature.exp:
Thomas More is a social philosopher, English lawyer, author and statesman.
He wrote the book named 'Utopia'. It is also known as Kingdom of Nowhere.
The book was originally written in Latin in 1516.

Source: An ABC of English Literature - Dr M Mofizar Rahman.

English Literature.question: ২৯) Which one is the first revenge tragedy in English literature?
English Literature.exp:
Thomas Kyd, (baptized Nov. 6, 1558, London, Eng.—died c. December 1594, London), English dramatist.
He in his The Spanish Tragedy (sometimes called Hieronimo, or Jeronimo, after its protagonist), initiated the revenge tragedy of his day.
Kyd anticipated the structure of many later plays, including the development of middle and final climaxes.
Source: Britannica.com

English Literature.question: ৩০) The speaker in a poem or novel is called -
English Literature.exp:
Persona:
The speaker in a poem or novel. The speaker is necessarily not the writer of the poem or novel.
For example -
The persona of Tennyson's 'Ulysses' is Ulysses, the Greek hero, not Tennyson.

Protagonist:
One who takes the leading part in a drama; hence, one who takes lead in some great scene, enterprise, conflict, or the like.
Antagonist:
One who contends with another, especially in combat; an adversary; an opponent.
Soliloquy:
An act of speaking one's thoughts aloud when by oneself or regardless of any hearers, especially by a character in a play.

Source: An ABC of English Literature - Dr M Mofizar Rahman

English Literature.question: ৩১) ‘Poetry’ serves the main genre of which literary period?
English Literature.exp:
Main Literary Features of The Middle English Period:
- Poetry serves as the main genre.
- Prose in English gets a strong foundation.
- The English Language reaches a considerable standard though old spelling continues.
- Drama began in the form of 'Mystery Play', 'Morality Play' and 'Interlude'.
Source: An ABC of English Literature, Dr M Mofizar Rahman.

English Literature.question: ৩২) Who is called the poet of poets in English literature?
English Literature.exp:
Edmund Spenser: (1552 - 99)
- He is called the 'Poet of poets' because many later English poets followed his art of poetry.
Some of his literary works:
- The Faerie Queene
- The Shephard's Calendar etc.

Source: An ABC of English Literature - Dr M Mofizar Rahman

English Literature.question: ৩৩) Among the University wits, who is not trained in a university?
English Literature.exp:
University Wits:
Elizabethan Period - এর একদল নাট্যকার (Dramatist) - কে একত্রে University Wits বলা হয়।
এই নাট্যকারদের প্রায় সবাই Oxford বা Cambridge University এর গ্রাজুয়েট।
তারা তাদের লেখনীতে গতানুগতিক ধারা পরিহার করে বৈচিত্র্য ও সমসাময়িক আধুনিকতা আনায়ন করেন।

University Wits - রা হচ্ছেনঃ
1. Christopher Marlowe - (Cambridge)
2. Robert Greene - (Cambridge)
3. Thomas Nashe - (Cambridge)
4. Thomas Lodge - (Oxford)
5. George Peele- (Oxford)
6. John Lyly - (Oxford)
7. Thomas Kyd (not university-trained)

University Wits - দের মধ্যে Christopher Marlowe কে Father of Tragedy বলা হয়।
তিনি Blank Verse উন্নতি ঘটান যা প্রায় পরবর্তী ৫০ বছর পর্যন্ত English Theatre কে নতুন ধারা তৈরি করে দেয়।

Source: Britannica.com ও An ABC of English Literature - Dr. M Mofizar Rahman।

English Literature.question: ৩৪) “An Apology for Poetry” is written by -
English Literature.exp:
Sir Philip Sidney was an Elizabethan courtier, statesman, soldier, poet, and patron of scholars and poets considered the ideal gentleman of his day.
After Shakespeare’s sonnets, Sidney’s Astrophel and Stella is considered the finest Elizabethan sonnet cycle.
His other literary works are:
- An Apology for Poetry/The Defence of Poesie (a critical treatise)
- Arcadia (1590), a book that bears the embryo of the English novel.

Source: Britannica.com ও An ABC of English Literature - Dr. M Mofizar Rahman।

English Literature.question: ৩৫) A brief and witty statement which is apparently self - contradictory is called -
English Literature.exp:
Epigram: (তীক্ষ্ণ, বুদ্ধিদীপ্ত বা ব্যঞ্জনাময় উক্তি; ক্ষুদ্র শ্লেষসমৃদ্ধ কবিতা বিশেষ।)
A brief and witty statement which is apparently self - contradictory.
Ex:
'Our sweetest songs are those that tell of saddest thought'.
Here, Sweetest and Saddest oppose each other but as we go beneath the surface level.

Paradox: (কূটাভাস; যে উক্তি আপাতদৃষ্টিতে স্ববিরোধী মনে হলেও সত্যবর্জিত নয়)
A self-contradictory statement that hides a rational meaning.
Ex: 'Sweet are the uses of adversity'.

Source: An ABC of English Literature - Dr M Mofizar Rahman

English Literature.question: ৩৬) “Tamburlaine the Great” is a play written by -
English Literature.exp:
Tamburlaine the Great, first play by Christopher Marlowe, produced about 1587 and published in 1590.
- The play was written in two parts, each of which has five acts, and was based on the earlier Silva de varia lección (1540; The Foreste; or, Collection of Histories) by the early 16th-century Spanish scholar and humanist Pedro Mexía.

Marlowe's other literary works are:
- Doctor Faustus,
- The Jew of Malta,
- Edward II,
- Didu,
- Queen of Carthage,
- The Massacre of Paris etc.

Source: Britannica.com ও An ABC of English Literature - Dr. M Mofizar Rahman।

English Literature.question: ৩৭) ''Charity begins at home, and justice begins next door'' - is a famous quote by:
English Literature.exp:
Charles Dickens, was an English novelist, generally considered the greatest of the Victorian era.
His famous quote - 'Charity begins at home, and justice begins next door.'
Source: Britannica.com

English Literature.question: ৩৮) 'Cordelia' is an important character in which Shakespear’s literary work -
English Literature.exp:
King Lear, tragedy in five acts by William Shakespeare, written in 1605–06 and published in a quarto edition in 1608, evidently based on Shakespeare’s unrevised working papers.

The aging King Lear decides to divide his kingdom among his three daughters, allotting each a portion in proportion to the eloquence of her declaration of love.
The hypocritical Goneril and Regan make grand pronouncements and are rewarded;
Cordelia, the youngest daughter, who truly loves Lear, refuses to make an insincere speech to prove her love and is disinherited.
Source: Britannica.com

English Literature.question: ৩৯) A statement in which there is a sudden fall from the serious to the trivial -
English Literature.exp:
Anti-climax/Bathos:
A statement in which there is a sudden fall from the serious to the trivial or from sublime to the ridiculous.

Climax:
The peak of importance in a play or in a story. It is the point at which the rise of action ends and fall of action begins.
Catastrophe:
Catastrophe is the dreadful consequence of the story of a tragedy. It is the final scene in which the action ends with the death of the hero and other characters.

Source: An ABC of English Literature - Dr M Mofizar Rahman

English Literature.question: ৪০) “First Folio” is the compilation of the literary works of -
English Literature.exp:
First Folio, first published edition (1623) of the collected works of William Shakespeare, originally published as Mr. William Shakespeares Comedies, Histories & Tragedies.
It is the major source for contemporary texts of his plays.
Source: Britannica.com

English Literature.question: ৪১) “Campaspe” a literary work of John Lyly is a/an -
English Literature.exp:
Campaspe is an Elizabethan era stage play, a comedy by John Lyly based on the life of Campaspe.
John Lyly is a University Wit.
His other famous works-
- Campaspe,
- Sapho and Phao,
- Midas etc.
Source: An ABC of English Literature, Dr. M Mofizar Rahman and Britannica.com

English Literature.question: ৪২) Who is considered to be the greatest satirist in English literature?
English Literature.exp:
Jonathan Swift is an Anglo-Irish author, who was the foremost prose satirist in the English language.

Jonathan Swift is best known for Gulliver’s Travels, which, in parodying the popular travel narrative, mocks English customs and the politics of the day,
and “A Modest Proposal,” a satiric essay that suggests improving living conditions in Ireland by butchering children of the Irish poor and selling them as food to wealthy English landlords.
His other literary works are:
- “A Tale of a Tub”
- 'Journal to Stella”
- “Drapier’s Letters”
- 'The Conduct of the Allies”

Source: Britannica.com

English Literature.question: ৪৩) “The Way of the World” is a literary work of -
English Literature.exp:
William Congreve (1670 - 1729) is a writer of The Restoration Period.
His literary works are:
- The Double Dealer
- Love for Love
- The Way of the World

All for Love - is a famous literary work of John Dryden.

Source: An ABC of English Literature - Dr M Mofizar Rahman

English Literature.question: ৪৪) Who wrote the novel 'Tom Jones'?
English Literature.exp:
Henry Fielding regarded as 'Father of English Novel'.
His novels are:
- Tom Jones,
- Amelia,
- Joseph Andrews,
- Jonathan Wilde,
- Top Secret.

Samuel Richardson wrote the first English novel 'Pamela' or 'Virtue Rewarded'.

Source: An ABC of English Literature - Dr M Mofizar Rahman

English Literature.question: ৪৫) “To spend too much time in studies is sloth” a quote of -
English Literature.exp: This is a quote of Francis Bacon and taken from his book “Of Studies”.

English Literature.question: ৪৬) “An Essay on Criticism” written by Alexander Pope is a/an -
English Literature.exp:
An Essay on Criticism, didactic poem in heroic couplets by Alexander Pope, first published anonymously in 1711 when the author was 22 years old.

Alexander Pope, (born May 21, 1688, London, England—died May 30, 1744, Twickenham, near London), poet and satirist of the English Augustan period.
He is best known for his mock heroic poetry.
Some of his famous works are:
- The Rape of the Lock (1712–14),
- The Dunciad (1728), and
- An Essay on Man (1733–34).
He is one of the most epigrammatic of all English authors.

Source: Britannica.com

English Literature.question: ৪৭) “Lovewit” is a character created by -
English Literature.exp:
'Lovewit' is an important character of the play 'The Alchemist' which is written by Ben Jonson.

The Alchemist is a comedy in five acts by Ben Jonson, performed in 1610 and published in 1612.
The play concerns the turmoil of deception that ensues when “Lovewit” leaves his London house in the care of his scheming servant, “Face”.
With the aid of a fraudulent alchemist named “Subtle” and his companion, “Dol Common”, Face sets about dispensing spurious charms and services to a steady stream of dupes.

Ben Jonson, byname of Benjamin Jonson is an English Stuart dramatist, lyric poet, and literary critic.
He is generally regarded as the second most important English dramatist, after William Shakespeare, during the reign of James I.

Source: Britannica.com

English Literature.question: ৪৮) Who is known as “Metaphysical Poet”?
English Literature.exp:
Metaphysical poet, any of the poets in 17th-century England who inclined to the personal and intellectual complexity and concentration that is displayed in the poetry of John Donne, the chief of the Metaphysicals.
Other Metaphysical poets are:
- Henry Vaughan,
- Andrew Marvell,
- John Cleveland,
- Abraham Cowley
- George Herbert and
- Richard Crashaw.

Source: Britannica.com

English Literature.question: ৪৯) A Shakespearean sonnet is divided into __ quatrains followed by a couplet.
English Literature.exp:
Sonnet:
A lyric poem of fourteen iambic pentameter lines.
It is of three types:
1. Petrarchan
2. Shakespearean and
3. Spenserian.

- The first eight lines of a Petrarchan Sonnet are called octave and the last six lines of it are called the sestet.
- A Shakespearean Sonnet is divided into three quatrains followed by a couplet. The concluding couplet is often used as a comment on the preceding lines.
- The Spenserian sonnet is named after Edmund Spenser who developed a different rhyme scheme for his sonnet. Like a Shakespearean sonnet, it consists of three quatrains followed by a couplet but the rhyme scheme differs from that of Shakespearean.

Source: An ABC of English Literature - Dr M Mofizar Rahman

The main characters in the poem are God, Lucifer (Satan), Adam, and Eve.

She is considered to be the anti-romantic novelist in the Romantic Age.

She published four novels during her lifetime:

- Pride and Prejudice (1813),

Mansfield Park, a novel by Jane Austen, published in three volumes in 1814.

English Literature.question: 61) “Lyrical Ballads” is published in -
English Literature.exp:
Lyrical Ballads, collection of poems, first published in 1798 by Samuel Taylor Coleridge and William Wordsworth, the appearance of which is often designated by scholars as a signal of the beginning of English Romanticism.
The work included Coleridge’s “Rime of the Ancient Mariner” and Wordsworth’s “Tintern Abbey,” as well as many controversial common-language poems by Wordsworth, such as “The Idiot Boy.”
The “Preface” to the second edition (1800) contains Wordsworth’s famous definition of poetry as the “spontaneous overflow of powerful feelings” and his theory that poetry should be written in “the language really used by men.”

Source: Britannica.com

Unsuccessful upon publication, the book is now considered a classic of American fiction and has often been called the Great American Novel.

To the Lighthouse, a novel by Virginia Woolf, published in 1927.
The work is one of her most successful and accessible experiments in the stream-of-consciousness style.

‘গীতাঞ্জলি’ ১৯১০ সালে গ্রন্থাকারে প্রকাশিত। এর ইংরেজী অনুবাদ - Song Offerings প্রকাশিত হয় ১৯১২ সালের নভেম্বরে ইংল্যান্ড থেকে।
অনুবাদ করেন কবি নিজেই এবং এর ভূমিকা লিখেন আইরিশ কবি W. B Yeats।
এই গ্রন্থের জন্য রবীন্দ্রনাথ প্রথম ভারতীয় হিসাবে ১৯১৩ সালে সাহিত্যে নোবেল পুরস্কার লাভ করেন।
উৎসঃ বাংলা ভাষা ও সাহিত্য জিজ্ঞাসা-ড. সৌমিত্র শেখর
W. B. Yeats ১৯২৩ সালে সাহিত্যে নোবেল পুরস্কার লাভ করেন।

English Literature.question: 95) “The Gift of the Magi” is a Short story by -
English Literature.exp:
O. Henry (William Sydney Porter):
American short-story writer.
Works:
The Gift of the Magi
The Last leaf
Cabbages and Kings
The Ransom of the Red Chief
The voice of the city
The four million.

English Literature.question: 96) ‘The Adventures of Huckleberry Finn’ is a Novel by -
English Literature.option4: ঘ) A and C both are correct
English Literature.exp:
Samuel Langhorne Clemens is the real name of Mark Twain.
His famous works: Life on the Mississippi, The Adventures of Huckleberry Finn(Novel), The Adventures of Tom Sawyer (Novel).
[Source: An ABC of English Literature, Dr M Mofizar Rahman and Britannica.com]

English Literature.question: 97) ‘Animal Farm’ was written by -
English Literature.exp:
George Orwell এর আসল নাম হলো Eric Arthur Blair. তিনি ব্রিটিশ ভারতে জন্মগ্রহণ করেন। Animal Farm এবং Nineteen Eighty Four জর্জ অরওয়েলের দুটি বিখ্যাত উপন্যাস।
Works:
Novel:
Animal Farm (1945 – a fairy story)
Nineteen Eighty-Four
Burmese Days
Coming up for Air.
Story/Essay: Shooting an Elephant, A Hanging.
Source: Encyclopedia Britannica.

English Literature.question: 98) Who is famous for his ‘Theory of Objective Correlative’?
English Literature.exp:
Thomas Stearns Eliot(1888-1965):
- He is an American Born British poet Dramatist and Social Critic.
- He is famous for his Theory of Objective correlatives.
- He is best known as a leader of the Modernist movement in poetry.
The famous poem of T.S. Eliot are:
The Waste Land, Gerontion, Journey to the Magi, Ash Wednesday, Four Quarters, The Hollow Man, Portrait of a Lady.
His famous drama is Murder in Cathedral, The Family Reunion, The Cocktail Party, The Elder Statement.
Source: An ABC of English Literature - Dr. M Mofizar Rahman.

English Literature.question: 99) Ulysses - is a Poem by -
English Literature.exp:
Lord Alfred Tennyson was a Victorian Poet. He is best known for his melodious language. He was a famous literary figure of the Victorian Age.
Poems, In Memoriam, Maud and Other Poems are his notable works.
His famous poems are - Oenone, Ulysses, Lotus Eaters, Locksley Hall, Tears Idle Tears, Tithonus, The Two Voices, The Lady of Shalott, Vision of Sin, Morte D'Arthur, etc.
Source: An ABC of English Literature, Dr M Mofizar Rahman and Britannica.com

জেনে রাখা ভাল,
Ulysses আইরিশ কবি ও ঔপন্যাসিক James Joyce রচিত বিংশ শতাব্দীর অন্যতম শ্রেষ্ঠ উপন্যাসও বটে।
James Joyce তার `Stream of Consciousness’ (চেতনার অন্তঃশীল প্রবাহ) টেকনিকের জন্যে বিখ্যাত।

English Literature.question: 100) ‘Hector Malone’ is the character of-
English Literature.exp:
Hector Malone হলো জর্জ বার্নার্ড শ রচিত Man and Superman নাটকের চরিত্র। এই নাটকের অন্যান্য চরিত্রগুলো হলো Ann Whitefield, John Tanner, Mendoza প্রমুখ।
